text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Enhanced Communications Network (Pvt) Ltd has withdrawn its application to the High Court requiring government to grant it a license to operate a private cellular telephone network on the understanding that three operators will now be licensed.

- Zimbabwe's first speaker of Parliament Didymus Mutasa has taken his successor Nolan Makombe to the Supreme Court challenging a decision taken by the House in 1993 to reprimand him for breach of parliamentary privilege.
- President Robert Mugabe has called on governments, opposition parties and non-governmental organisations to work together in mapping out strategy to educate society.

- The independent candidate in Harare's Ward 6 Avenues, Priscilla Misihairabwi, was on Wednesday disqualified because she was said to be under-age but was requalified on Thursday when she produced copies of a new birth certificate and national identity card altering her date of birth.

- The growing scandal involving Zimbabwe's first head of state, Reverend Canaan Banana (61) intensified with the announcement that attorney-general Patrick Chinamasa will investigate allegations of sexual abuse against the former president saying he is not immune to prosecution.

- The country's clothing industry, which has lost 10,000 jobs over the past five years, will shrink by a further 50 percent if the new tariff regime announced last week is implemented as it is, the Zimbabwe Clothing Council (ZCC) has said.

- Results of HIV tests conducted in Zimbabwe may in some cases not be accurate following increasing reports of people who have undergone tests for the HIV virus that causes Aids through different medical centres and have obtained contradictory results.
